analysis:
The only changed file is scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py, a CI workflow-lint unit test. It ships in no provider runtime, so the changes touch no provider assets, no coordinator-to-provider boundary and no key custody. I found no regression against the canonical threat model (T-041 and the others).

The test file now pins two workflow behaviors that the same PR presumably implements in .github/workflows/* and .github/actions/*/action.yml. Those files are not in the supplied units.

1. VALIDATE_GIT (head lines ~152-187) now discards a restored cached .git when it is not a directory, holds a symlink or a non-sample hook, or its config sets core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or an include. This hardens the CI cache-poisoning path. A fork or PR could otherwise poison a .git cache and gain code execution at checkout on macOS runners.
   - Limits I noticed: the config check inspects only files named config or config.worktree; it does not check global or system config; and the grep matches only the listed key prefixes. Other executing keys (core.sshCommand, filter.*.process, diff.external, credential.helper and similar) are not filtered. That is a hardening gap in the CI script, outside the provider threat model. I did not raise it as a finding because the real workflow YAML was not supplied.
   - The `find -exec git config --file` step parses config files only. It does not execute anything.

2. CACHE_GATE (CI_ACTIONS_CACHE) skips every actions/cache step on a Darkbloom Sandbox runner that has no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. This prevents sandbox jobs from reading or writing GitHub's own cache, which could poison refs/heads/master. The test asserts the gate on every cache step in all workflows and actions, and exercises the gate script across runner and URL combinations.

Open question for integration: whether the real workflow YAML matches the pinned strings (VALIDATE_GIT, CACHE_GATE_RUN, gated conditions). The test file only asserts them, so the YAML is where enforcement actually happens. That YAML is outside the supplied evidence.

The patch excerpt is truncated but the head and base ranges are complete, and I saw no further security-relevant changes.
